[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DAST-2.7.08.md#abb-context]

### ABB Context

- **Parent L2 Capability**: Application Security Testing — [GUID-SEC-APP-CAP-DESC-1.7.02](../GUID-SEC-APP-CAP-DESC-1.7.02.md)
- **ABB Catalog**: [GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-CAT-2.7.06](../GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-CAT-2.7.06.md)
- **Capability Statement**: The enterprise SHALL have an architectural capability to probe running application instances for exploitable security weaknesses by simulating external attacker behavior against live endpoints.
page_texts.4:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DAST-2.7.08.md#abb-scope]

### ABB Scope

**In Scope**:
- Architectural capability to send crafted requests to a running application and analyze responses for indicators of vulnerability
- Integration into pre-production pipeline stages where a deployed application instance is available
- Finding correlation and reporting to development and security teams

**Out of Scope**:
- Source code analysis without execution (see GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SAST-2.7.07)
- In-process instrumentation of running applications (see GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-IAST-2.7.09)
- Manual penetration testing (an operational security activity outside pipeline scope)
- Security controls, tool selection, or configuration baselines (`standards/security/`)

[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DAST-2.7.08.md#core-principles]

### Core Principles

- DAST capability SHALL target a deployed application instance in a non-production environment that is representative of the production configuration.
- DAST SHALL be integrated into the pipeline at a stage after successful deployment to a test environment.
- Findings SHALL be triaged and tracked with the same severity taxonomy used for SAST findings to enable unified reporting.
- DAST SHOULD be scoped to authenticated application paths as well as unauthenticated endpoints.
page_texts.8:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DAST-2.7.08.md#active-scanning]

#### Active Scanning

**Architectural intent**: Identify runtime-exploitable vulnerabilities by probing application endpoints with attack-class inputs.

**Design guidance**:
- Scanning SHALL cover at minimum web application attack classes relevant to the application's technology profile.
- Scan scope SHALL be defined to avoid unintended impact on shared test environments or data.
- Authentication credentials for authenticated scan paths SHALL be managed through the Secrets Vault ABB (GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-VAULT-2.7.21).
page_texts.9:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DAST-2.7.08.md#pipeline-integration]

#### Pipeline Integration

**Architectural intent**: Ensure dynamic testing occurs at a consistent, automated point before promotion to production.

**Design guidance**:
- DAST SHALL be triggered automatically after a successful deployment to a designated test environment.
- Findings above a defined severity threshold SHOULD block promotion unless an approved exception exists.
- Scan results SHALL be retained and associated with the pipeline run for traceability.
page_texts.10:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DAST-2.7.08.md#integration-interfaces]

### Integration Interfaces

| Interface | Direction | Consuming ABB | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pipeline Trigger | Inbound | CI/CD Pipeline | Receives deployment completion event to initiate scan |
| Target Application | Outbound | Running Application Instance | HTTP/HTTPS traffic sent to application endpoints |
| Findings Output | Outbound | GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-CAT-2.7.06 | Structured findings for gate logic and tracking |
page_texts.11:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DAST-2.7.08.md#zero-trust-alignment-nist-sp-800-207]

### Zero Trust Alignment (NIST SP 800-207)

DAST advances the Applications and Workloads pillar by validating that deployed application instances cannot be externally exploited, reinforcing the assumption that network position alone does not confer trust.
page_texts.12:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DAST-2.7.08.md#nist-sp-800-53-intent-alignment]

### NIST SP 800-53 Intent Alignment

This ABB enables the architectural intent of the CA (Assessment, Authorization, and Monitoring) family — specifically the intent that security assessments are performed on operational systems — and the SI family, which addresses flaw identification and remediation.
page_texts.13:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DAST-2.7.08.md#constraints-and-dependencies]

### Constraints and Dependencies

- DAST requires a running, accessible application instance; it cannot be applied to code that has not been deployed.
- Scan duration must be considered in pipeline design; long-running scans may require asynchronous execution patterns.
- DAST and SAST are complementary; DAST alone does not provide coverage of code paths not reachable from external interfaces.
